semantic_fragments.content: If the CLINICAL THERMOMETER cannot indicate a temperature within the LABORATORY ACCURACY, it either provides a TECHNICAL ALARM CONDITION or it does not provide an OUTPUT TEMPERATURE. Minimum RATED OUTPUT RANGE of the CLINICAL THERMOMETER is from 34°C to 42°C. Actual rated output range: 32.0°C to 42.9°C.

CLINICAL THERMOMETERS intended for home healthcare use require the display of OUTPUT TEMPERATURE of at least 4mm or the value is optically magnified to this height. This is indicated in USABILITY ENGINEERING PROCESS. Actual display height: 10mm.

Laboratory performance is assessed in DIRECT MODE or in TEST MODE under the same conditions. Alternatively correction method is used to derive unadjusted temperatures from OUTPUT TEMPERATURE in accordance with the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT. Tested in test mode.

CLINICAL ACCURACY VALIDATION: ADJUSTED MODE CLINICAL THERMOMETER are VALIDATED for CLINICAL ACCURACY in each ADJUSTED MODE in accordance with ISO 14155-1:2003 and ISO 14155-2:2003. The results of CLINICAL ACCURACY VALIDATION is disclosed in the ACCOMPANYING DOCUMENT. Requirements cover: human subject population (febrile subjects 30-50%, minimum 105 total, minimum 35 per age group, minimum 15 in A1 or A2); age groups A1 (0-3 months), A2 (3-12 months), B (>1 and <5 years), C (>5 years); Clinical Bias (∆cb); Limits of Agreement (LA); Clinical Repeatability (σr). All marked N/E in this report.
Electromagnetic compatibility (clause 201.17, IEC 60601-1:2005 Clause 17) is not evaluated in this report. ME SYSTEMS (clause 201.16) is not applicable as the device is not an ME system.
